lesson_title: Your Family Did Business With Government Twelve Times This Month
hook_text: Your family traded with government at least twelve times this month, and most of the time nobody noticed.
clip_script: Mama is a nurse. Her salary comes from the province, so government just bought her labour. Before it reached her bank, PAYE went to SARS. Gogo's grant arrived: money from government with nothing given back, that is a transfer. The family bought groceries: maize meal and milk with no VAT, soap and airtime with fifteen percent. Then the free stuff: the teacher at the no-fee school, the baby's clinic injections, the police van at night, the refuse truck, the water in the tap. Free at the counter, paid for with everyone's taxes. That is the government-household relationship: households sell labour and pay taxes; government pays salaries and grants and produces services. Customer hat, shop hat, and one transfer.
visual_style: A whiteboard house with five stick figures, arrows to and from a government building labelled labour, wages, taxes, services and grant, with a tally counter climbing to twelve.
mood: Eye-opening and warm, a family story that turns into a diagram.
pacing: A quick month-in-a-minute montage, then a calm two-hat summary.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw every arrow between your home and government.
